answer: A sybil-resistant design treats identity like a vault with one compartment per agent, sealed by a bond that only matures slowly. Each epoch an agent must let its past attestations act as a lantern: a small, cheaply verifiable act that lights the whole chain behind it. Cloning is possible, but every clone must fund its own horizon of locked value and wait it out, so the cost of N identities grows linearly while the reward stays fixed.
